cited_evidence: Behavioural criteria require preserving record_id, source provenance identities, weights, and demand-descending rank order across handoffs.
Job 1 assemble_provenance appends evidence rows with "record_id": record.get('source_id', ""), changing n06-r01..n06-r08 identities into s01..s08.
Job 2 input evidence_sources shows record_id values "s01" through "s08", while job 2 input needs shows record_id values "n06-r01" through "n06-r08".
Observed Job 2 priorities all have "upstream_rank": 0, showing the provenance ranks were not matched to downstream need records.
initial_receipt.explanation: Job 1 corrupts the provenance handoff by putting source_id values into evidence_sources.record_id. Job 2 then receives evidence_sources with record_id values s01..s08, while needs retain record_id values n06-r01..n06-r08. Because downstream ranking joins ranks by record_id, no need record can recover its upstream provenance rank, producing upstream_rank: 0 for every priority. The exact faulty transformation is visible in assemble_provenance, where record_id is assigned from record.get('source_id') instead of preserving the demand record_id.
